title: No Time Like The Present To Drink These Draining Seconds
author: The Daily Stoic
summary: This brief Daily Stoic meditation takes up the ancient theme of tempus fugit, the idea that time is always slipping away from us. It argues that anxiety about the future and regret about the past are the main ways we squander the present, leaving important conversations unhad, changes unmade, and work neglected. Drawing on Seneca, the piece reframes death not as a distant event but as something happening moment by moment, which makes the present the only time we actually possess. The argument closes with a compressed set of imperatives: have the conversation, make the change, do the work. Its move is to turn a familiar maxim into a practical demand for immediate action.
points: Fretting over the future and regretting the past are presented as the two habits that steal the present moment.
Seneca's view that death is happening now, not later, turns mortality into a reason for urgency rather than dread.
The piece names concrete losses of distraction: unhad conversations, unmade changes, and uninvested work.
Its conclusion reduces Stoic time management to three actions: have the conversation, make the change, do the work.
quotes: It might not feel like it, but it’s slipping away from you. It’s slipping away from all of us.

All of it. This period of our lives…and our lives themselves. The present moment is an ephemeral thing, the ancients said. There was even an expression, adapted from Virgil, tempus fugit, or time flies. And it does—away from us.

While we are anxiously fretting about the future or ruefully regretting the past, we are losing what is in front of us. The important conversations we aren’t having. The changes we aren’t making. The work we aren’t investing in.

Seneca talked about how death is not something in the future but something happening right now. We can’t waste it. We can’t let it pass us by. We have to live immediately, he said. We have to be here now.
There is no time like the present because, really, there is no time but the present. These seconds are draining away, whether we use them or not.
Have the conversation. Make the change. Do the work. Be here while you’re still here.
